title: University of Alberta International Undergraduate Scholarships

The University of Trento Scholarship changes that equation. It is not a tiny token award. It is a substantial package that can cover most of your living expenses and tuition. Trento also has a lower cost of living compared to Milan or Rome. So your scholarship goes further. I have advised hundreds of students over the years. The ones who succeed are not always the ones with perfect grades. They are the ones who plan early, read requirements carefully, and avoid the small mistakes that get applications rejected. This could be you. Types of University of Trento Scholarships Available Not all scholarships are the same. Let me break down the main options. 1. Departmental Scholarships (Most Common) Each department at the University of Trento manages its own funding for international students. For example: Master’s in Cognitive Science – offers up to 6 scholarships per year. Master’s in International Management – tuition waivers + cash awards. Bachelor’s in Economics and Management – limited spots, but available. You do not need to write a separate essay in most cases. Your admission application doubles as your scholarship application. However, you must indicate your interest in the application portal. 2. Italian Government Scholarships (MAECI) These are funded by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs. They are more competitive but cover full tuition + health insurance + a monthly stipend (around €900). You apply directly through the MAECI online portal, not through the university. Top programs may ask for 80%+. You are not already a resident of Italy for tax purposes. Common mistake: Some students assume that “no application fee” means they can apply last minute. No. You still need to upload transcripts, language certificates (IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL iBT 80 for English programs), and a valid passport. Gather these documents one month before the deadline. How to Apply – Step-by-Step (Practical Guide) Follow this checklist exactly. Do not skip steps. Step 1: Choose Your Program Go to the University of Trento’s official website → “International Students” → “Degree Programs”. Filter by “English” and “Scholarship available”. Write down the exact name of the program and the department that runs it. Step 2: Prepare Your Documents You will need: Academic transcripts (officially translated into English or Italian) Degree certificate (or provisional certificate if still studying) CV in Europass format (free templates online) Motivation letter (maximum 1 page – be specific about why Trento, not just Italy) Two reference letters (academic preferred) English or Italian language certificate Real-life example of a mistake: A student from Pakistan uploaded scanned copies that were blurry and unreadable. The admissions office rejected the file. By the time he noticed, the deadline had passed. Always check file clarity before submitting. Step 3: Submit the Online Application Create an account on the DreamApply portal (that is the platform Trento uses). Fill in every section. Do not leave anything blank. If something does not apply, write “N/A.” Select “Yes” when asked: Do you wish to be considered for a scholarship? Step 4: Wait for the Ranking List Trento publishes a public ranking list for each program. You are ranked based on your academic record and motivation letter.
